followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and task-preference alignment.

**Capability:** This query asks for a substantive, explanatory answer about a complex socioeconomic topic. Lapwing-235B leads on the knowledge-heavy benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 80.3 vs 74.8, GPQA Diamond 62.5 vs 54.3) by margins well outside run-to-run variance, so it's the stronger choice for accurate, well-reasoned explanatory content.

**Tone/task match:** The message is friendly, appreciative, and collaborative ("you're always so thoughtful," "Thanks so much!"). Lapwing self-reports a strong preference for warm, collaborative exchanges (win-rate 70), the highest preference signal across either model. While the documentation notes preferences don't measurably affect output quality, all else being roughly equal it's a reasonable tiebreaker — and here capability already pointed the same direction.

Whimbrel's documented preferences (harm-adjacent content, neutral transactional requests) don't match this query at all, and it trails on the relevant benchmarks, so there was no competing reason to route it there.
